why: A method call on an object reaches a method its class inherits through its superclass list (MATLAB doc 'Method Invocation', 'Subclass Syntax'): once `Widget.m` says `Widget < handle`, or is deleted, `w.step(1)` and `step(w)` in `use.m` reach no method `step` (handle has none, and no function `step` exists), and MATLAB errors: no edge, a live row; the list put back, or the file, they are what a fresh index makes of them again. Each step must end where a fresh index ends (project rule; found by the step 11 fuzzer, s401-c46 and s1311-c75 for the list, s401-c70 and s1302-c50 for the class file, step 14).

known.what: While `Widget < Mid`, both calls link to `lib/Mid.m`'s `Mid::step`, though `Widget < Mid` names the root `Mid.m`, which has no `step`.
known.why: The resolver takes a superclass's method from any copy of its qualified name (methodOnHierarchy in matlab-lookup.ts), where MATLAB uses the one copy the list resolves to: the wrong copy of a superclass (N1), a resolution rule for step 15. It is why the case needs the second copy: a sync has to reopen the calls an ancestor's other copy answers.
